solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Blowing his top, awkward person makes you jump

indicators.note: losing one's top means losing the head, so the opening letter of the word goes

blocks.note: a klutz is a clumsy, awkward person

explanation.surface: A clumsy man loses his temper and startles everyone around him.
explanation.walkthrough: KLUTZ without its top letter K leaves LUTZ. 'Blowing his top' reads as an angry outburst, but it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutz is a figure-skating leap taken from a backward outside edge, named after the skater Alois Lutz.

clue.text: Magic drug, not a thing helping save Romeo

indicators.note: save here means except, so the letter named after it is excluded

blocks.note: nothing at all, the tennis score for zero
a helping of food is a portion
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A magic drug lacking a key ingredient that might have rescued Shakespeare's Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTION loses its R to become POTION. The surface pulls towards Romeo and Juliet, where a sleeping draught fails to save the hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A love potion is the classic enchanted brew of folklore, supposed to make the drinker fall for someone.

clue.text: Give encouraging cry during ecstasy

indicators.note: something happening during another sits within its span, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Spanish shout of encouragement at a bullfight or dance
an ecstatic state is a trance

explanation.surface: An instruction to cheer someone on while they are in raptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in the give in a rope or a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Give as a noun is the allowable slack or play in something, which engineers call tolerance.

clue.text: Song mostly probing a writer’s devastation

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
a probe pushes into something, so one piece is inserted into another

blocks.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song
taken as written
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A song that digs into an author's ruin or despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the American Edgar Allan Poe; the apostrophe-s after writer only links the parts and adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is a catastrophic event of total destruction, so it stands for devastation on a grand scale.

clue.text: Catch it in carp’s close season

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept
in places one piece inside the other pieces

blocks.note: final letter of the fish
taken as written
fall is the American name for autumn

explanation.surface: An angler told to land a carp during the closed fishing season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close season' is a real angling term, the months when fishing is banned, which hides that close only picks one letter and season is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden snag or drawback, and a pitfall is likewise an unsuspected danger or trap.

clue.text: Part of a church’s fortune, land primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: fortune in the sense of luck
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A church's wealth consists chiefly of the land it owns.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition borrows the apostrophe-s of church, which the surface reads as possession of fortune and land.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the eastern area around the altar, reserved for clergy and choir, so it is one section of the building.

clue.text: Maybe the tower of Pisa’s special property

blocks.note: first meaning, read playfully: a structure that lists, or leans
second meaning: a building given protected status for its historic interest

explanation.walkthrough: To list is to lean, as a ship does, so the famous leaning tower is a 'listed' building in a joking sense; in Britain a listed building is one officially protected from alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage law in Britain puts notable structures on a register, making them protected property that owners cannot freely alter.

clue.text: Religious leader in prison over debts

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever stands at its front, so its first letter is taken

blocks.note: first letter of the word
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A cleric jailed because of the money he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious leader' looks like the definition, but leader belongs to the wordplay; in a down clue 'over' puts the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious describes a person devoutly observant in faith, so it serves as a synonym for religious.

clue.text: Only some dared enter paradise

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a run lifted from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Few people had the nerve to walk into heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of dared and the start of enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived, the archetype of an earthly paradise.

clue.text: Swimmers ignoring the youngest’s higher priorities

definitions.note: a cryptic reading of the phrase

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: fish apart from the very young ones, which are called fry
second meaning: the idiom for more important matters to attend to

explanation.surface: A shoal of fish paying no attention to their newest offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: Fry are newly hatched fish, so swimmers that are not the youngest are fish other than fry; the apostrophe-s joins the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Having other fish to fry is the idiom for having more important business demanding your attention.

clue.text: Plain or extremely loud check trousers

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremes of a word, its two end letters
trousers is a verb here: to trouser something is to pocket it, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Choosing between plain trousers and a garish checked pair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads loud check trousers as a fashion choice; trousers is the verb, meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: The veldt is the open grassland of southern Africa, a flat expanse of country, hence a plain.

clue.text: Switch stance on gender identity

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: short for transgender, a gender identity
a stance or posture

explanation.surface: A politician changing position on gender identity questions.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the first piece after the second, so the stance follows the identity.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpose things is to swap their order or positions, which is what switching them means.

clue.text: Italian food in her canapé seems unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it doubles as part of the signal

explanation.surface: An Italian ingredient looks out of place on her party snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The word seems does double duty, supplying letters while also forming part of the signal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard grating cheese from the Parma region of Italy, an example of Italian food.

clue.text: Gully regularly covered by mad prophet’s rock carving

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken
mad means crazed or disordered, so the letters are jumbled
to be covered by something is to be wrapped inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An unhinged seer's carving in a rocky ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: The prophet's letters are rearranged and then wrap the three picked from gully; the apostrophe-s after prophet just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A petroglyph is a prehistoric image cut into a rock surface, from the Greek for stone and carving.

clue.text: Glad that husband has left plenty of petrol

indicators.note: someone who has left is no longer present, so that letter disappears

blocks.note: glad and grateful
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife relieved that her husband has driven off with a full tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has left' reads as departing, perhaps leaving fuel behind, but it removes a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankful is the amount a fuel tank holds, which is a good quantity of petrol.

clue.text: Like sage and thyme, albeit a blend

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two herbs that are good together in a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A blend' sounds like a herb mixture, but the a is fodder and blend is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Labiate plants belong to the mint family, with lipped flowers; sage and thyme are both members.

clue.text: Appeal to drop the act and admit it is harassment …

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so those letters are removed
to admit is to let in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: appeal as in charm or allure
the word itself, minus the article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to stop pretending and own up that this behaviour is harassment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue, whose own wordplay also involves dropping it; the surface reads as one appeal across both.
explanation.definitionFit: Attrition is a wearing down by constant pressure, as in a war of attrition, which is what harassment of an enemy does.

clue.text: Run drugs deliveries in batches at first

indicators.note: at first marks which piece is put in front of the other in the chain

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a batch of six balls delivered by one bowler
E is ecstasy, so two of them

explanation.surface: A dealer running drugs, with deliveries done in small lots to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests a drug courier, but it is cricket, where a bowler delivers six balls per over. 'At first' sends that piece ahead of the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an operation is to manage or supervise it, which is to oversee it.

clue.text: … just dropping it would be level-headed

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall away, so those letters are lost

blocks.note: just in the sense of fair
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: simply letting the matter go would be the calm response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'simply' in the surface, but it means fair and supplies the long word.
explanation.definitionFit: An equable person is even-tempered and calm, never easily upset, which is what level-headed describes.

clue.text: Party, hard one to fit into schedule

indicators.note: to fit into something is to slot inside it

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a rota or timetable of duties

explanation.surface: A party that is difficult to squeeze into a busy diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party, hard one' tempts a split after party with hard as H, but the definition is 'party hard', and no H appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily and boisterously, so it means to party hard as a verb.

clue.text: Short end of the stick of green wood

blocks.note: inexperienced or unripe
deal is sawn pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A stick of unseasoned wood, snapped short at one end.
explanation.walkthrough: The stick and wood seem to belong together, but the stick is part of the idiom; deal is a British word for softwood planks.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the short end of the stick is an idiom for unfair treatment, just as a raw deal is.

clue.text: Union forced to raise legitimate issue

definitions.text: Union forced to raise legitimate issue

blocks.clueFragment: Union forced to raise legitimate issue
blocks.note: surface reading: a trade union obliged to bring up a fair grievance
setter's reading: a marriage pushed through so that a child, the issue, is born legitimate

explanation.walkthrough: Union suggests organised labour and issue a grievance, but issue also means offspring, and union a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names a marriage hurried through because the bride is pregnant, notionally at a father's gunpoint.

clue.text: Hard currency put together by a scavenger

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
the Japanese currency
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hard cash scraped together by someone who picks through rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard currency' is a financial phrase, so splitting it into two pieces is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are African carnivores famous for feeding on carcasses killed by other animals.

clue.text: At a wake, stand and drink to an auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is judged by how it is heard

blocks.note: a common drink, said the same way

explanation.surface: At a funeral gathering, mourners rise and raise a glass to an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand and drink' reads as a toast, but stand is the noun definition. An auditor is usually an accountant; here it is just someone listening.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the movable frame on which a coffin or corpse rests before burial, a stand seen at a wake.

clue.text: Fine comic story, so good I can’t tell you

definitions.text: so good I can’t tell you

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are played about with

blocks.note: taken as written
a fable is a moral tale

explanation.surface: Praising a funny tale as beyond words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic story' looks like one phrase, but comic works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffable means too great or extreme to be expressed in words, so something so good it cannot be described.

clue.text: Piercing? One’s unduly curious about it

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: prying or nosey
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone with a new piercing asks why another person is so nosy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Piercing suggests a nose ring, but it is an adjective for a loud sound; 'it' points back to the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing sound is shrill and loud enough to hurt, so it is a noisy one.

clue.text: Dishes for heating synthetic emerald, say

indicators.note: something synthetic is artificially made up, so the letters are reconstructed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Heating a man-made emerald in a dish, perhaps in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it marks an example, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready meals are pre-cooked supermarket dinners that need only warming in an oven or microwave.

clue.text: Small island bird’s beginning to disappear

indicators.note: the beginning disappearing means the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird on a tiny island that is starting to vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in many place names; the apostrophe-s on bird stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch, from Gaelic innis, is a small island, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth.
